 Spring Hill Fire Dept. Awarded Gary Sinise Foundation Grant 
 By apearson@mainstreetmediatn.com 
 on 
 November 18, 2026 
 LUCAS WRIGHT 
 City of Spring Hill 
 Spring Hill Fire Department purchased an augmented reality fire extinguisher training system thanks to a grant from the Gary Sinise Foundation. LUCAS WRIGHT 
 The Spring Hill Fire Department (SHFD) has been awarded a $17,474 grant through the Gary Sinise Foundation First Responder Outreach Program to purchase an augmented reality fire extinguisher training system.
 The grant will fund the FiAR Fire Extinguisher Training System V2, an augmented reality training tool that allows trainees to practice fire suppression using real hardware in any indoor or outdoor environment without messy chemical discharge, cleanup or reset times.
 “We understand the work your department performs daily is imperative to the safety and security of the citizens of Spring Hill and surrounding areas,” said Madisen Gentry Moore, Director of Community Outreach for the Gary Sinise Foundation. “Gary, the Gary Sinise Foundation, and our thousands of American donors from across the country are honored to be able to assist you. We hope this equipment helps keep your first responders safe and assists them in their life-saving day-to-day work.”
 SHFD does not have a fire extinguisher training device for demonstrations or public education. The previous device was outdated and did not function correctly. It was disposed of in 2024.
 Bringing the FiAR system in house allows easy access to training exercises for residents — furthering the goal of the Community Risk Reduction program within SHFD.
 “This amazing technology takes advantage of augmented reality to bring realistic live training to any location for actual hands-on experience,” said Chief Graig Temple. “Our Community Risk Reduction efforts extend beyond messaging and fire safety best practices; if you, your workplace, or community group would like to demo this device and get the hands-on training, contact Captain Lisa Burns.”
 The Spring Hill Board of Mayor and Aldermen voted to accept the grant funding by way of Resolution 26-281 on Oct. 5.
